title: Protesters block Orange Order march on Garvaghy Road in Portadown

tea.why: Residents protested against a planned Orange Order march along Garvaghy Road, a route barred to them for nearly 30 years.
tea.want: To stop the Orange Order march from proceeding down Garvaghy Road.
tea.changed: Oct 10: Northern Ireland Secretary Chris Bryant banned the contentious march after talks failed.

summary: A multi-day standoff and protest took place in Portadown, Northern Ireland, after the Orange Order attempted to march down Garvaghy Road following a court ruling. The planned procession was blocked by republican protesters, including First Minister Michelle O’Neill, starting on September 27. The area had previously been a major flash point during the Troubles, and residents of the traditionally nationalist area argued the march was provocative. Following weeks of stalemate and a request from the Police Service of Northern Ireland Chief Constable, Northern Ireland Secretary Chris Bryant intervened and officially banned the procession on Friday night, citing a lack of compromise. The Orange Order subsequently launched a legal challenge at the High Court in Belfast.
demands: Prevent the Orange Order parade along Garvaghy Road
response: Northern Ireland Secretary Chris Bryant banned the procession after talks failed, calling for all protests and rallies to be stood down. (Sources: 1, 2)

updates.text: Protesters blocked Orange Order members from carrying out their planned march along Garvaghy Road.
Northern Ireland Secretary Chris Bryant banned the march following a two-week standoff.
The Orange Order challenged the government's decision at the High Court in Belfast.
